title: Exec staff meeting prep notes - 2026-03-06
content:
Context: Weekly exec staff sync (30m). Goal: align on top risks (latency/cost), Dedicated renewals, Private onboarding pilot, headcount ask for SRE, and a short decision on model fallbacks policy.

Attendees: CEO, CTO, VP Eng, VP Product, Head of SRE (Michael Chen), Head of Sales Ops (Priya Sharma)

Proposed agenda (30m):
- 0:00 - 0:03 Quick status + wins (ops: 99.95% uptime last week, hosted API QPS +8%)
- 0:03 - 0:10 Metrics deep-dive (latency, cost, quality regressions)
- 0:10 - 0:16 Dedicated renewals + pricing decision for ACME Corp pilot
- 0:16 - 0:22 Private deployment pilot status (onboarding blockers)
- 0:22 - 0:26 Headcount ask: SRE +2 (on-call coverage & runbook improvements)
- 0:26 - 0:30 Decisions & next steps (including model fallback policy)

Metrics & talking points to surface:
- Latency: P95 token latency (hosted) = 210ms (target 180ms). P99 = 720ms. Notable tail spikes correlate with long-seq requests from partner integrations.
- Cost: Avg cost per 1k tokens up 6% month-over-month due to more long-response completions and lower batching efficiency for small chat flows. Redwood Optimize suggestions to increase batching/windowing for low-priority routes ready for pilot.
- Errors: 0.6% 5xx for streaming endpoints last 7 days; root cause traced to a retry bug in gateway when backend partial-evictions occur. Patch planned this week.
- Quality: Two eval prompt sets show a minor regression on model X v1.3 vs v1.2 (semantic paraphrase score -2.1%). Holding rollout for traffic >10% until rollback or mitigation.

Key asks / discussion points:
1) Decision: Approve revised Dedicated pilot pricing for ACME (proposal in linked PR). Need sign-off to convert PoC to committed reserved capacity.
2) Approval: Headcount (SRE +2) to reduce on-call load and shorten incident MTTR. Budget impact: ~ $340k annual.
3) Guidance: Model fallback policy — do we allow automatic fallback to quantized variants for latency SLO breaches, or require manual approval per customer? (Tradeoff: reliability vs. slight quality drop).
4) Escalation: Private onboarding pilot (BankCo) hitting network config hurdles; need legal & infra alignment on encryption/KMS SLA.

Risks / blockers:
- If we push auto-quantized fallbacks without per-customer opt-out, we risk perceived quality regressions for enterprise customers.
- Sales pipeline: ACME expects 4 wks to contract signature once pricing cleared; any delay pushes revenue into next quarter.
- Private pilot needs a dedicated infra engineer for 2 weeks to resolve VPC peering and KMS rotation.

Prepared one-slide metrics summary: (bring numbers only)
- Hosted API: QPS +8% WoW, P95 210ms, P99 720ms, 5xx 0.6%
- Dedicated: Utilization 72% (target 70-85%), queued requests increased during spike window
- Private: BankCo pilot blocked on KMS rotation & peering (see linked ticket)
- Costs: +6% MoM per-1k-token unit

Draft decisions we should aim to close in the meeting:
- Approve ACME pilot pricing (Y/N)
- Approve SRE headcount hire (Y/N)
- Interim fallback policy: allow auto-fallback for non-enterprise customers for up to 15% traffic, enterprise require opt-in/explicit sign-off

Follow-ups / action items (owner; due):
- Michael Chen; Due 2026-03-10; Action: Provide incident runbook update and proposed on-call roster for +2 hires (include budget lines).
- Priya Sharma; Due 2026-03-09; Action: Coordinate with Sales to notify ACME timeline and confirm pricing lever acceptance; surface any contract objections.
- Noah Li; Due 2026-03-08; Action: Draft auto-fallback policy doc (short POA) and recommended telemetry flags for rollout gating; include rollback criteria.
- Ava Thompson; Due 2026-03-07; Action: Confirm resource allocation for Private pilot (assign infra engineer for 2 weeks) and open KMS SLA thread with Legal.
- Eng infra (owner TBD); Due 2026-03-12; Action: Patch gateway retry bug and run canary for streaming endpoints (target reduction of 5xx to <0.2%).

Notes / talking points for CEO/CTO:
- Emphasize that small config changes to batching can materially reduce per-token cost; propose Redwood Optimize pilot on top 20 routes.
- Recommend we tie Dedicated renewals to utilization thresholds and offer a test-burst incentive for ACME to reduce purchase friction.
- Stress need to finalize fallback policy quickly to prevent ad-hoc operator decisions during incidents.

Prep attachments to share in meeting: linked_artifacts above + one-pager metrics slide (internal).

Quick personal notes (for speaking):
- Open with "operational wins" (uptime + positive QPS trend), then quickly move to the 3 decision asks. Keep ask framing: revenue (ACME), reliability (SRE hires + retry patch), product risk (fallback policy).

End.
